title: How Tibo Louis-Lucas built TMAKER to $1M/month by making distribution the moat
summary: Tibo explains how two failed VC-funded startups taught him to validate by revenue, ship many small products, and use equity deals with influencers. He now acts as the distribution operator across five SaaS products with co-makers, using reusable SEO, ads and influencer systems. He also candidly regrets selling Tweet Hunter and Taplio.

principles.text: Validate with revenue, not downloads or active users; look for people paying again in month two.
principles.quote: we were looking only at revenue to see if people were interested enough to put their credit cards and pay for it.

principles.text: Strongest demand signal: signups and subscriptions arriving when you do no promotion.
principles.quote: if you don't tweet, don't post on Reddit, like do nothing during the day and still get some new signups and subscription, this is another very strong signal.

principles.text: Real product-market fit is demand that is hard to serve, not comfortable growth.
principles.quote: I think that this is the true product market fit. It's when you get so much demands that it's getting hard to serve.

principles.text: Ship many cheap products to get a baseline; one product gives you no reference for what good traction looks like.
principles.quote: People need to ship more to get more reference of what's a good product.

principles.text: Reusable distribution systems (ads pipeline, SEO playbook, influencer network) can power every product, so the distribution operator scales better than the maker.
principles.quote: You can build an ads pipeline, you can build an SEO playbook, you can build an influencer network and every single product can benefit from those systems.

principles.text: With AI making building easy, product success will be decided mostly by distribution; SEO captures the highest-intent leads and lasts.
principles.quote: with AI making building so easy, I wanted to go into the distribution space because I think this is where it's all going to play.
